def solve_cvrp(instance):
    depot = instance["depot_index"]
    customer_ids = instance["customer_ids"]
    demands = instance["demands"]
    capacity = instance["capacity"]
    matrix = instance["distance_matrix"]

    # If any demand exceeds capacity, no feasible solution exists under constraints.
    # Still return something deterministic: each customer in its own route if possible, else empty.
    customers = [c for c in customer_ids if c != depot]
    for c in customers:
        if demands[c] > capacity:
            # Can't satisfy feasibility; return empty routes (deterministic).
            return [[] for _ in range(max(1, instance.get("vehicle_count_hint", 1)))]

    # ---------- Helper functions ----------
    def route_load(route):
        s = 0
        for n in route:
            s += demands[n]
        return s

    def route_cost(route):
        if not route:
            return 0
        c = matrix[depot][route[0]] + matrix[route[-1]][depot]
        for a, b in zip(route[:-1], route[1:]):
            c += matrix[a][b]
        return c

    def total_cost(routes):
        s = 0
        for r in routes:
            s += route_cost(r)
        return s

    # ---------- Clarke-Wright savings (deterministic) ----------
    # Start with singleton routes
    routes = []
    route_loads = []
    # For each customer, track (route_index, position, orientation end)
    # position = 0 means at start, -1 means at end in the stored list
    pos_in_route = {}  # customer -> (rid, at_start_bool, at_end_bool)

    for c in customers:
        rid = len(routes)
        routes.append([c])
        route_loads.append(demands[c])
        pos_in_route[c] = (rid, True, True)

    # Savings sorted deterministically: by (saving desc, i asc, j asc)
    savings = []
    n = len(customers)
    for ii in range(n):
        i = customers[ii]
        di0 = matrix[depot][i]
        for jj in range(ii + 1, n):
            j = customers[jj]
            s = di0 + matrix[depot][j] - matrix[i][j]
            savings.append((s, i, j))
    savings.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[1], x[2]))

    # Max merges: conservatively bounded by number of customers to avoid long loops
    merges_done = 0
    max_merges = len(customers) - 1 if len(customers) > 0 else 0

    for _, i, j in savings:
        if merges_done >= max_merges:
            break
        ri, i_start, i_end = pos_in_route[i]
        rj, j_start, j_end = pos_in_route[j]
        if ri == rj:
            continue

        # Allow merge only if i and j are at appropriate ends (to keep simple list concatenations)
        # Case 1: i at end of its route, j at start of its route => route_i + route_j
        # Case 2: i at start, j at end => route_j + route_i (i becomes appended after j)
        can_merge = False
        merged_route = None
        merged_load = None

        if i_end and j_start:
            li = route_loads[ri]
            lj = route_loads[rj]
            if li + lj <= capacity:
                can_merge = True
                merged_route = routes[ri] + routes[rj]
                merged_load = li + lj
                # New route stored in ri position, rj removed
                keep_rid = ri
                drop_rid = rj
        elif i_start and j_end:
            li = route_loads[ri]
            lj = route_loads[rj]
